Theme

Latin word

dēclīnātiō

dēclīnātiō, dēclīnātiōnis f.

noun, third declension

the conjugation of a verb; any inflection; declension; any inflection of a word

In this lexicon

  • conjugation

    also used · classical · Quint. 1.4.29: multa verba nōn tōtum dēclīnātiōnis ōrdinem ferunt; Varr. LL 8.2 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 245; Traupman 295; Traupman 332

  • declension

    the recommended word · classical · Varr. LL 8.2 (Lewis & Short); Quint. 1.5.63; 1.6.5; Traupman 222, 246; M-O s.v. declension; Traupman 239; Traupman 302; Traupman 332

Examples

  • nōmina dēclīnāre et verba in prīmīs puerī sciant, neque enim aliter pervenīre ad intellēctum sequentium possunt

    above all, let boys know how to decline nouns and verbs, for they cannot otherwise come to understand what followsQuint. 1.4.22

    In the entry for declension

  • comparātiō in nōminibus aut genus dēprehendit aut dēclīnātiōnem; … dēclīnātiōnem, ut sī veniat in dubium, hāc domū dīcendum sit an hāc domō et domuum an domōrum

    in nouns, comparison settles either the gender or the declension: the declension, when it is doubtful whether to say hāc domū or hāc domō, domuum or domōrumQuint. 1.6.5

    In the entry for declension

    In the entry for declension
